correctness.summary: Conditioning on the selected coordinate and stale-read delay gives an exact closed scalar recurrence for the diagonal-scaled second moment. Its nonnegative companion matrix and a strictly increasing root equation identify the Perron factor. Stochastic/convex-order monotonicity follows from convexity of q^{-D}; the deterministic-delay and near-singular asymptotics follow by logarithmic and Taylor expansions. A standalone script independently checks the root equation against direct iteration of the scalar recurrence.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Older work establishes broad asynchronous convergence theory, stochastic-delay state augmentation, first-moment rate models, and randomized asynchronous Gauss-Seidel bounds. Moga--Dubois (1995) explicitly studies two-variable stochastic-delay rate matrices for the expected trajectory, while Avron--Druinsky--Gupta (2015) and Peng--Xu--Yan--Yin (2019) provide broader bounds. Searches did not locate the exact second-moment scalar closure here, its arbitrary bounded-delay root law, convex-order comparison, fixed-mean extremizers, or the stated near-singular expansion. Residual risk remains because the full Beidas--Papavassilopoulos (1993) paper and the recent Carson--Ma preprint arXiv:2609.15605 were not inspected in full.

value.summary: The result supplies an exactly solvable benchmark for asynchronous randomized Gauss-Seidel in which the full delay distribution, rather than only a maximum-delay bound, determines the rate. It separates mean-delay and variability effects, gives worst and best fixed-mean bounded delay laws, and quantifies the large-delay and ill-conditioned regimes.

limitations: Coordinate selection is uniform and independent.
Stale-read delays are independent, identically distributed, bounded, and independent of the iterate history.
Updates are exact coordinate overwrites; relaxation parameters and inconsistent multi-coordinate reads are not covered.
The exact recurrence concerns a diagonal-scaled mean-square norm rather than the A-energy.
The full text of Beidas--Papavassilopoulos (1993) was not inspected; a specialized prior corollary remains a residual originality risk.
The full text of Carson--Ma arXiv:2609.15605 was not inspected; only its abstract was checked, leaving a contemporaneous-overlap risk.
Independent audit has not been performed.
